     6→## Overview

     8→A workflow binds a shell command (e.g., `npm run dev`, `python run.py`, `cargo run`) to a long-running task managed by Replit. Workflows are used to run webservers, background services, TUIs, and other persistent processes.

Good question — there's a real reason both exist. They are two **completely different Android permission systems** that do different jobs:

---

**Step 1 — "Gallery & Media Access"**
This is the standard Android runtime permission (`READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO`, `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`). It gives the app access to your phone's **general media storage** — the gallery, Downloads folder, etc. StatusVault needs this specifically to **save** a status into your gallery album. Without it, the "Save" button can't write anything to your phone.

**Step 2 — "WhatsApp Folder Access" (SAF)**
This is a completely separate Android mechanism called **Storage Access Framework**. WhatsApp stores its status files inside `/Android/media/com.whatsapp/WhatsApp/Media/.Statuses` — which is a **sandboxed, semi-private folder**. Starting on Android 11, Google blocked normal media permissions from reading inside `/Android/media/` at all. So even if Step 1 is granted, the app literally cannot see that folder. SAF is a second, independent folder-picker grant that specifically unlocks that path.

---

**In short:**
- Step 1 = permission to **write** to your gallery (save files out)
- Step 2 = permission to **read** from WhatsApp's protected folder (pick up status files coming in)

They are not duplicates. One handles the destination, the other handles the source. Android 11+ made both mandatory — there is no way around it on modern devices without both grants being given separately. That's why the screen shows both steps.

---

**What was broken (and why most status saver apps have this problem):**

When your app called `requestDirectoryPermissionsAsync`, Android broadcasts `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE`. Samsung MyFiles, MIUI File Manager, Realme, Vivo, and Oppo file managers have all registered themselves to intercept that broadcast — and they open at their own root home screen, ignoring the `EXTRA_INITIAL_URI` hint entirely.

---

**What was built — three layers of fix:**

**Layer 1 — New native `SafPickerModule.java`**
Instead of letting Android choose which file manager handles the intent, the module calls `intent.setPackage("com.android.documentsui")` — this directly names Android's built-in system document picker and forces it to handle the request. OEM file managers are completely bypassed. `com.android.documentsui` always respects `EXTRA_INITIAL_URI`.

**Layer 2 — Correct URI format**
Changed all SAF hint URIs from `/tree/` to `/document/` format. `EXTRA_INITIAL_URI` is documented to expect the `/document/` form — some OEM pickers that partially respected the hint were failing silently because of this wrong format.

**Layer 3 — `<queries>` in AndroidManifest**
Android 11+ has package visibility rules — an app can't detect or target another app's package without declaring it in `<queries>`. The new plugin adds `<package android:name="com.android.documentsui"/>` so the app can confirm DocumentsUI is available before targeting it, and gracefully fall back if it's not.
